title: introduce-invocation-context-vector-metrics-and-behavioral-alert-tuning
author: Anika Sharma
description: Summary: Add a compact per-invocation "context_vector" metric that fingerprints the semantic context immediately preceding generation and wire it into span/trace tags, dashboards, and a new behavioral alert weighting system. Motivation: many costly/ noisy alerts are driven by a small number of invocation classes (e.g., long-form summarization, code-generation harnesses). By grouping invocations by a lightweight context vector we can: 1) reduce alert noise via weighted scoring, 2) sample representative traces for high-novelty contexts, and 3) provide a searchable dashboard for drift and heavy-tail cost sources. Design: (a) extract a reduced-dim context vector from the last N tokens using the existing embedding pipeline with a projection to a 64-d float32 vector; (b) quantize into compact shard ids (context_vector_id) using locality-preserving hashing for low-cardinality metrics; (c) attach context_vector_id and a novelty_score tag to the trace/span metadata; (d) record aggregate metrics: telemetry.context_vector.count, telemetry.context_vector.cost_p50/p90/p99, telemetry.context_vector.novelty; (e) introduce behavioral alerter: alerts carry a context weighting function (higher weight for novel contexts and lower for stable, high-volume contexts). Implementation notes: the collector lives behind a feature flag (telemetry.context_vector.enabled) and defaults to off for Dedicated/Private clusters; sampling is bounded by per-tenant rate controls; quantization uses a tunable shard_count (default 1024). Rollout: staged canary on 10% of prod traffic for 48h then 50% for 72h, full roll on green. Backwards compatibility: context_vector is added as an optional span attribute; no change to existing SLI calculations. Testing: unit tests for vector extraction, end-to-end integration in the local perf lab with synthetic long-tail workloads, and a small eval job to verify reduced false-positive rate on alerting. Dashboard: adds a new 'Context Vector Explorer' dashboard with UMAP projections, per-shard cost heatmap, novelty timeline, and sample trace links. Operator controls: Console flag to flip feature, per-tenant quota controls in Dedicated, and a metric to track feature overhead (telemetry.context_vector.cpu_ms). Security/PII: only tokenized/context embeddings are used; we do not persist raw prompt text in the collector. See commits and changed files for details.

review_comments: Jason Li: Nice minimal surface. Two asks: make shard_count configurable per-tenant and add a hard CPU budget so this can't be used for free-form heavy processing.
Anika Sharma (reply): added per-tenant shard_count and tenant_cpu_budget config; default conservative values set; explained behavior in runbook.
Diane Park: Can we avoid embedding calls for small requests? Also call out the privacy review outcome.

Anika Sharma (reply): added request-size cutoff (token_count < 32 skips vector); privacy reviewed — we only store quantized shard ids and novelty floats, note added to docs/observability/context-vector-runbook.md.
Ravi Menon: CI perf job failed first run; re-ran and it passed. Suggest adding a perf baseline for 95th percentile CPU overhead.
Anika Sharma (reply): added perf baseline test and recorded baseline numbers in telemetry/dashboards/context_vector_explorer.json comments.

release_notes: Adds optional context_vector fingerprinting for invocations, a Context Vector Explorer dashboard, and a behavioral alert weighting mechanism to reduce false positives from stable high-volume invocation classes. Feature is behind a flag and off by default for Dedicated/Private until tenant config is applied.
